# --- Execution Step ---
df_array_ops = df_users.withColumn(
    "genre_count", F.size(F.col("genres"))
).withColumn(
    "likes_action", F.array_contains(F.col("genres"), "Action")
).withColumn(
    "primary_genre", F.element_at(F.col("genres"), 1)  # 1-based index: first
).withColumn(
    "last_genre", F.element_at(F.col("genres"), -1)     # negative index: last
).withColumn(
    "sorted_genres", F.array_sort(F.col("genres"))
)

df_array_ops.select("user_id", "genre_count", "likes_action", "primary_genre", "last_genre", "sorted_genres").show(truncate=False)

# --- Execution Step ---
# Simulate secondary recommendations array

df_sets = df_with_recs.withColumn(
    "all_genres_union", F.array_distinct(F.array_union(F.col("genres"), F.col("recommended_genres")))
).withColumn(
    "common_genres", F.array_intersect(F.col("genres"), F.col("recommended_genres"))
)

df_sets.select("user_id", "all_genres_union", "common_genres").show(truncate=False)

description: Develop a generic, production-ready recursive schema flattener in Python that traverses any arbitrarily deep Spark schema. The function must explode nested arrays and flatten all nested structs into top-level columns (`parent_child_field`).

from pyspark.sql import functions as F
from pyspark.sql import types as T
from pyspark.sql.window import Window

spark.sparkContext.setLogLevel("WARN")
print(f"Spark Version: {spark.version}")
print(f"Session Active: {spark.sparkContext.appName}")

# --- Execution Step ---
deep_data = [
    {
        "id": "ACC-99",
        "company": {
            "name": "Acme Corp",
            "headquarters": {
                "geo": {"lat": 37.7749, "lon": -122.4194},
                "city": "San Francisco"
            }
        },
        "metrics": {"financials": {"revenue": 5000000.0, "ebitda": 1200000.0}}
    }
]

import json
rdd_json = spark.sparkContext.parallelize([json.dumps(d) for d in deep_data])
df_deep = spark.read.json(rdd_json)
print("Original Deeply Nested Schema:")
df_deep.printSchema()

# --- Execution Step ---
def flatten_dataframe(df):
    """
    Recursively flattens all StructType columns in a DataFrame into top-level columns.
    """
    flat_cols = []
    has_struct = False

    for field in df.schema.fields:
        if isinstance(field.dataType, T.StructType):
            has_struct = True
            for child in field.dataType.fields:
                flat_cols.append(
                    F.col(f"{field.name}.{child.name}").alias(f"{field.name}_{child.name}")
                )
        else:
            flat_cols.append(F.col(field.name))

    df_result = df.select(*flat_cols)
    # If any struct columns were flattened, recurse until all structs are resolved
    if has_struct:
        return flatten_dataframe(df_result)
    return df_result

df_flattened = flatten_dataframe(df_deep)
print("Completely Flattened Schema:")
df_flattened.printSchema()
df_flattened.show(truncate=False)

# --- Execution Step ---
expected_cols = [
    "id",
    "company_name",
    "company_headquarters_city",
    "company_headquarters_geo_lat",
    "company_headquarters_geo_lon",
    "metrics_financials_ebitda",
    "metrics_financials_revenue"
]

for c in expected_cols:
    assert c in df_flattened.columns, f"Expected column {c} missing from flattened DataFrame"

print(f"Successfully flattened deep schema into {len(df_flattened.columns)} scalar columns!")
notes: Deeply nested schemas can cause severe query compilation overhead. Traversing the schema programmatically inspects `df.schema.fields` and constructs a projection expression list dynamically without executing any JVM actions.

from pyspark.sql import functions as F
from pyspark.sql import types as T
from pyspark.sql.window import Window

spark.sparkContext.setLogLevel("WARN")
print(f"Spark Version: {spark.version}")
print(f"Session Active: {spark.sparkContext.appName}")

# --- Execution Step ---
bad_json_lines = [
    '{"id": "EVT-1", "user": "alice", "score": 95}',
    '{"id": "EVT-2", "user": "bob", "score": INVALID_NUMBER}', # Malformed token
    '{"id": "EVT-3", "user": "charlie", "score": 82}',
    'NOT_EVEN_JSON_PAYLOAD',                                      # Completely unparseable
    '{"id": "EVT-4", "user": "diana", "score": 100}'
]

rdd_dirty = spark.sparkContext.parallelize(bad_json_lines)

# --- Execution Step ---
# Define schema including special corrupt record column
quarantine_schema = T.StructType([
    T.StructField("id", T.StringType(), True),
    T.StructField("user", T.StringType(), True),
    T.StructField("score", T.IntegerType(), True),
    T.StructField("_corrupt_record", T.StringType(), True)
])

# Read with PERMISSIVE mode
df_permissive = (
    spark.read
    .option("mode", "PERMISSIVE")
    .option("columnNameOfCorruptRecord", "_corrupt_record")
    .schema(quarantine_schema)
    .json(rdd_dirty)
)

print("Ingested Records with Quarantine Column:")
df_permissive.show(truncate=False)

# --- Execution Step ---
df_clean = df_permissive.filter(F.col("_corrupt_record").isNull()).drop("_corrupt_record")
df_dead_letter = df_permissive.filter(F.col("_corrupt_record").isNotNull()).select("_corrupt_record")

print(f"Clean Records: {df_clean.count()}")
df_clean.show()

print(f"Corrupted Dead-Letter Records: {df_dead_letter.count()}")
df_dead_letter.show(truncate=False)
notes: `PERMISSIVE` is Spark's default mode: corrupted fields evaluate to NULL and the unparseable string is diverted to `_corrupt_record`. `FAILFAST` halts execution immediately upon encountering syntax errors. `DROPMALFORMED` silently drops damaged records.
use_case: A public data ingestion pipeline scrapes third-party web endpoints. Up to 5% of incoming payloads contain syntax errors (truncated braces, mismatched quotes, non-JSON tokens). The pipeline must never crash and must capture all corrupted lines into an audit column.

clickstream = [

]

df_clicks.show()

# --- Execution Step ---
df_aggregated = df_clicks.groupBy("session_id").agg(
    F.collect_list("page_url").alias("all_pages_list"),
    F.collect_set("page_url").alias("unique_pages_set")
)

df_aggregated.show(truncate=False)

# --- Execution Step ---
# Pack timestamp and URL into struct: array_sort will sort by struct's first field (event_time)
df_sorted_journey = (
    df_clicks
    .groupBy("session_id")
    .agg(
        F.array_sort(F.collect_list(F.struct("event_time", "page_url"))).alias("sorted_struct_events")

        F.expr("transform(sorted_struct_events, x -> x.page_url)")

If a single key contains millions of entries (key skew), this can trigger severe Executor OutOfMemory (OOM) errors. from pyspark.sql import functions as F
from pyspark.sql import types as T
from pyspark.sql.window import Window

spark.sparkContext.setLogLevel("WARN")
print(f"Spark Version: {spark.version}")
print(f"Session Active: {spark.sparkContext.appName}")

# --- Execution Step ---
spending = [
    ("ACC-1", "2023-11-01", 120.0),
    ("ACC-1", "2023-11-02", 45.0),
    ("ACC-1", "2023-11-03", 210.0),
    ("ACC-1", "2023-11-04", 80.0),
    ("ACC-1", "2023-11-05", 15.0),
    ("ACC-1", "2023-11-06", 350.0),
    ("ACC-1", "2023-11-07", 90.0)
]

schema = "account_id STRING, txn_date STRING, amount DOUBLE"
df_spend = spark.createDataFrame(spending, schema)
df_spend.show()

# --- Execution Step ---
# Cumulative window from start to current row
cum_window = (
    Window.partitionBy("account_id")
    .orderBy("txn_date")
    .rowsBetween(Window.unboundedPreceding, Window.currentRow)
)

# 3-day moving window: 2 preceding rows plus current row
moving_window = (
    Window.partitionBy("account_id")
    .orderBy("txn_date")
    .rowsBetween(-2, Window.currentRow)
)

df_analytics = df_spend.withColumn(
    "cumulative_spend", F.round(F.sum("amount").over(cum_window), 2)
).withColumn(
    "moving_avg_3day", F.round(F.avg("amount").over(moving_window), 2)
)

print("Cumulative Spending & Moving Average Analysis:")
df_analytics.show()

# --- Execution Step ---
dup_data = [
    ("A", 1, 10.0),
    ("A", 2, 20.0),
    ("A", 2, 30.0),  # Duplicate order key
    ("A", 3, 40.0)
]
df_dup = spark.createDataFrame(dup_data, ["id", "val", "amt"])

# ROWS vs RANGE
w_rows = Window.partitionBy("id").orderBy("val").rowsBetween(Window.unboundedPreceding, Window.currentRow)
w_range = Window.partitionBy("id").orderBy("val").rangeBetween(Window.unboundedPreceding, Window.currentRow)

df_comp = df_dup.withColumn("sum_rows", F.sum("amt").over(w_rows))                .withColumn("sum_range", F.sum("amt").over(w_range))

print("Notice sum_range evaluates tied val=2 together into 60.0, while sum_rows evaluates row-by-row:")
df_comp.show()
notes: The default window frame for an ordered window is `RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW`. This can cause subtle bugs when duplicate order keys exist, as Spark aggregates all rows with the identical key together. Using `ROWS BETWEEN` guarantees explicit physical row framing.

from pyspark.sql import functions as F

from pyspark.sql.window import Window

spark.sparkContext.setLogLevel("WARN")
print(f"Spark Version: {spark.version}")
print(f"Session Active: {spark.sparkContext.appName}")

# --- Execution Step ---
subscription_history = [
    ("SUB-1", "2023-01", 100.0),
    ("SUB-1", "2023-02", 100.0),
    ("SUB-1", "2023-03", 150.0), # Upgrade
    ("SUB-1", "2023-04", 120.0), # Downgrade
    ("SUB-2", "2023-01", 50.0),
    ("SUB-2", "2023-02", 50.0),
    ("SUB-2", "2023-03", 0.0)    # Churn
]

schema = "sub_id STRING, billing_month STRING, mrr DOUBLE"
df_subs = spark.createDataFrame(subscription_history, schema)
df_subs.show()

# --- Execution Step ---
window_sub = Window.partitionBy("sub_id").orderBy("billing_month")

df_lag_lead = df_subs.withColumn(
    "prev_mrr", F.lag("mrr", 1, default=0.0).over(window_sub)
).withColumn(
    "next_mrr", F.lead("mrr", 1, default=0.0).over(window_sub)
)

df_lag_lead.show()

# --- Execution Step ---
df_variance = df_lag_lead.withColumn(
    "mrr_change", F.round(F.col("mrr") - F.col("prev_mrr"), 2)
).withColumn(
    "pct_change",
    F.when(F.col("prev_mrr") == 0, None)
     .otherwise(F.round(((F.col("mrr") - F.col("prev_mrr")) / F.col("prev_mrr")) * 100, 1))
).withColumn(
    "status_tag",
    F.when(F.col("prev_mrr") == 0, "NEW")
     .when(F.col("mrr") > F.col("prev_mrr"), "EXPANSION")
     .when((F.col("mrr") < F.col("prev_mrr")) & (F.col("mrr") > 0), "CONTRACTION")
     .when(F.col("mrr") == 0, "CHURNED")
     .otherwise("RETAINED")
)

df_variance.select("sub_id", "billing_month", "prev_mrr", "mrr", "mrr_change", "pct_change", "status_tag").show(truncate=False)
notes: Offset functions fetch values from neighboring rows within the same executor partition buffer without self-joining the table. Self-joins require a full Cartesian shuffle, whereas `lag()` operates in single-pass linear time $O(N)$ inside the partition.
use_case: A SaaS subscription billing service analyzes customer MRR (Monthly Recurring Revenue). Finance requires month-over-month revenue variance, detection of plan upgrades/downgrades, and churn identification when an active account drops subscription renewal.

title: #029 Sessionization and the Gaps & Islands Problem in PySpark
category: Advanced SQL, Aggregations & Analytical Window Functions
description: Solve the classic Gaps and Islands problem in distributed PySpark: detect temporal gaps using `lag()`, mark island session boundaries with conditional flags, compute cumulative sums over flags to generate sequential session IDs, and aggregate session metrics.
code:
import os
import sys
import shutil
from pathlib import Path

# In Databricks, the SparkSession 'spark' is pre-initialized by the cluster.
# For local PySpark / CI execution, initialize a local session with Delta Lake support:
try:
    spark
except NameError:
    from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
    spark = (
        SparkSession.builder
        .appName("UseCase_029_Sessionization_and_the_Gaps_and_Islands_Problem_in_PySpark")
        .master("local[*]")
        .config("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "4")
        .config("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "true")
        .config("spark.sql.extensions", "io.delta.sql.DeltaSparkSessionExtension")
        .config("spark.sql.catalog.spark_catalog", "org.apache.spark.sql.delta.catalog.DeltaCatalog")
        .getOrCreate()
    )

from pyspark.sql import functions as F
from pyspark.sql import types as T
from pyspark.sql.window import Window

spark.sparkContext.setLogLevel("WARN")
print(f"Spark Version: {spark.version}")
print(f"Session Active: {spark.sparkContext.appName}")

# --- Execution Step ---
clicks = [
    ("U-01", "2023-11-20 10:00:00", "/home"),
    ("U-01", "2023-11-20 10:12:00", "/catalog"),     # 12 min gap (same session)
    ("U-01", "2023-11-20 10:25:00", "/product/42"),  # 13 min gap (same session)
    ("U-01", "2023-11-20 11:30:00", "/home"),        # 65 min gap -> NEW SESSION!
    ("U-01", "2023-11-20 11:40:00", "/cart"),        # 10 min gap (same session)
    ("U-02", "2023-11-20 09:00:00", "/login"),
    ("U-02", "2023-11-20 09:15:00", "/dashboard")
]

schema = "user_id STRING, event_time STRING, page STRING"
df_raw_clicks = spark.createDataFrame(clicks, schema).withColumn("ts", F.to_timestamp("event_time"))
df_raw_clicks.show(truncate=False)

# --- Execution Step ---
user_window = Window.partitionBy("user_id").orderBy("ts")

df_gaps = df_raw_clicks.withColumn(
    "prev_ts", F.lag("ts").over(user_window)
).withColumn(
    "inactivity_minutes",
    F.coalesce((F.col("ts").cast("long") - F.col("prev_ts").cast("long")) / 60.0, F.lit(0.0))
).withColumn(
    "is_new_session",
    F.when((F.col("inactivity_minutes") > 30.0) | (F.col("prev_ts").isNull()), 1).otherwise(0)
)

df_gaps.select("user_id", "event_time", "inactivity_minutes", "is_new_session").show()

# --- Execution Step ---
cum_session_window = Window.partitionBy("user_id").orderBy("ts").rowsBetween(Window.unboundedPreceding, Window.currentRow)

df_sessionized = df_gaps.withColumn(
    "session_num", F.sum("is_new_session").over(cum_session_window)
).withColumn(
    "session_id", F.concat(F.col("user_id"), F.lit("_SESS_"), F.col("session_num"))
)

print("Sessionized Clickstream:")
df_sessionized.select("session_id", "user_id", "event_time", "page", "inactivity_minutes").show(truncate=False)

# Aggregate session summaries
df_summary = df_sessionized.groupBy("session_id", "user_id").agg(
    F.min("ts").alias("session_start"),
    F.max("ts").alias("session_end"),
    F.count("page").alias("page_views"),
    F.round((F.max("ts").cast("long") - F.min("ts").cast("long")) / 60.0, 1).alias("session_duration_min")
)

print("Aggregated Session Profiles:")
df_summary.show(truncate=False)
notes: Solving Gaps & Islands in Spark uses a 2-step window pattern: (1) An ordered window with `lag()` to compute time delta between consecutive events and emit a 1/0 boundary indicator, and (2) A cumulative sum window over the boundary indicator to generate monotonic session IDs across the entire partition.
use_case: A digital analytics platform tracks web page views. An active browsing session is defined as consecutive clicks separated by no more than 30 minutes of inactivity. When a gap exceeds 30 minutes, a new unique session identifier must be generated.

        condition="target.sku = source.sku"
    )
    .whenMatchedDelete(
        condition="source.quantity = -999"
    )
    .whenMatchedUpdate(
        set={
            "quantity": F.col("source.quantity"),
            "unit_price": F.col("source.unit_price"),
            "last_updated": F.col("source.last_updated")
        }
    )
    .whenNotMatchedInsert(
        values={
            "sku": F.col("source.sku"),
            "product_name": F.col("source.product_name"),
            "quantity": F.col("source.quantity"),
            "unit_price": F.col("source.unit_price"),
            "last_updated": F.col("source.last_updated")
        }
    )
    .execute()
)

print("Target Table after MERGE INTO:")
target_table.toDF().orderBy("sku").show()
notes: Delta MERGE is an atomic operation that performs a full outer join between source updates and target Delta files to identify matching keys. It rewrites only the specific files containing matching rows, avoiding full table rewrites.
use_case: A retail inventory management system synchronizes daily inventory updates from 500 physical warehouses. If an item exists in the central inventory table, update stock quantity and last_restocked date; if missing, insert the new SKU; if stock drops to -999 (discontinued), delete the item.

parquet_base_path = "/tmp/parquet_legacy_043"

# --- Execution Step ---

# Incoming Record: {"device_id": "IOT-99", "temp": "INVALID_FLOAT", "new_feature": "GPS_ACTIVE"}
# Target Schema: device_id STRING, temp DOUBLE
#
# Auto Loader Output:
# device_id: "IOT-99"
# temp: NULL
# _rescued_data: '{"temp": "INVALID_FLOAT", "new_feature": "GPS_ACTIVE"}'

print("Auto Loader _rescued_data architecture mapped.")

# Mock incoming data with mismatched types and extra columns
raw_stream = [
    ("D-1", "25.5", "NORMAL"),
    ("D-2", "CORRUPTED_TEMP", "CRITICAL"),
    ("D-3", "30.0", "NORMAL")
]

# Resilient parsing capturing unparseable values in rescued_data
clean_expr = F.expr("try_cast(raw_temp AS DOUBLE)")

df_rescued = df_raw.withColumn("temp", clean_expr).withColumn(
    "_rescued_data",
    F.when(
        F.col("temp").isNull() & F.col("raw_temp").isNotNull(),
        F.to_json(F.struct(F.col("raw_temp"), F.lit("Type mismatch: expected DOUBLE").alias("error_reason")))
    ).otherwise(None)
)

print("Parsed Records with Rescued Data Capture:")
df_rescued.select("device_id", "temp", "status", "_rescued_data").show(truncate=False)

# --- Execution Step ---
autoloader_options = {
    "cloudFiles.format": "json",
    "cloudFiles.schemaEvolutionMode": "addNewColumns",  # Options: addNewColumns, rescue, failOnNewColumns
    "cloudFiles.inferColumnTypes": "true",
    "cloudFiles.schemaRescuePath": "/tmp/schema_rescue"
}

print("Production Auto Loader Evolution Settings:")
for k, v in autoloader_options.items():
    print(f"  {k} = '{v}'")

Any values that cannot be parsed into the existing schema (e.g. string arriving in integer column) are automatically diverted into the JSON `_rescued_data` column, ensuring zero data loss.

        raw_path = spec["raw_path"]
        target_path = spec["target_path"]
        partition_cols = spec.get("partition_cols", [])
        options = spec.get("options", {})

        print(f"--> Ingesting {table_name} [Format: {fmt}] from {raw_path}")

        # 1. Read dynamically using format and options
        reader = self.spark.read.format(fmt)
        for k, v in options.items():
            reader = reader.option(k, v)
        df_raw = reader.load(raw_path)

        # 2. Add standard audit columns
        df_enriched = (
            df_raw
            .withColumn("_ingested_at", F.current_timestamp())
            .withColumn("_source_file", F.input_file_name())
            .withColumn("_batch_id", F.lit(datetime.utcnow().strftime("%Y%m%d%H%M%S")))
        )

        # 3. Write standardized Delta table
        writer = df_enriched.write.format("delta").mode("append")
        if partition_cols:
            writer = writer.partitionBy(*partition_cols)
        writer.save(target_path)

        count = df_enriched.count()
        print(f"--> Successfully landed {count} records into {target_path}")
        return df_enriched

print("UnifiedIngestionEngine class ready.")

# --- Execution Step ---
# Prepare sample files
with open("/tmp/src_orders_050.json", "w") as f:
    f.write('{"order_id": "O1", "amount": 120.0, "order_status": "COMPLETED"}\n')
    f.write('{"order_id": "O2", "amount": 85.0, "order_status": "PENDING"}\n')

with open("/tmp/src_products_050.csv", "w") as f:
    f.write("prod_id,prod_name,cost\nP1,Widget,10.50\nP2,Gizmo,25.00\n")

engine = UnifiedIngestionEngine(spark)
for spec in pipeline_specs:
    engine.ingest(spec)

print(f"Session Active: {spark.sparkContext.appName}")

# --- Execution Step ---

import io

zip_dir = Path("/tmp/zip_archives_052")
if zip_dir.exists():
    shutil.rmtree(zip_dir)
zip_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

# Create a zip file containing 2 inner CSV files
zip_path = zip_dir / "quarterly_reports.zip"
with zipfile.ZipFile(zip_path, "w") as zf:
    zf.writestr("q1_sales.csv", "report_id,amount\nR1,500.0\nR2,800.0\n")
    zf.writestr("q2_sales.csv", "report_id,amount\nR3,650.0\nR4,920.0\n")

print(f"Created sample ZIP archive at {zip_path}")

# --- Execution Step ---
# binaryFiles returns (file_path, PortableDataStream)
rdd_binary = spark.sparkContext.binaryFiles(str(zip_dir))

def extract_zip_entries(tuple_item):
    file_path, byte_stream = tuple_item
    records = []
    # Read bytes into ZipFile in memory on executor
    with zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(byte_stream)) as z:
        for inner_filename in z.namelist():
            if inner_filename.endswith(".csv"):
                content = z.read(inner_filename).decode("utf-8")
                lines = content.strip().split("\n")
                # Skip header, extract rows
                for line in lines[1:]:
                    parts = line.split(",")
                    records.append((inner_filename, parts[0], float(parts[1])))
    return records

# Distributed flatMap extracts files across cluster executors
rdd_extracted = rdd_binary.flatMap(extract_zip_entries)
df_decompressed = spark.createDataFrame(rdd_extracted, ["archive_member", "report_id", "amount"])

print("Decompressed Records Extracted in Parallel:")
df_decompressed.show()

# --- Execution Step ---
codecs = [
    ("GZIP (.gz)", "No", "High", "Text / Web Logs", "Cannot split without container format"),
    ("BZIP2 (.bz2)", "Yes", "Very High", "Cold Archival", "Splittable via 48-bit sync markers"),
    ("SNAPPY", "Yes (in Parquet/Avro)", "Medium", "Active Analytics", "High-speed decompression"),
    ("ZSTD", "Yes (in Parquet)", "Very High", "Modern Lakehouse", "Balanced compression and speed"),
    ("ZIP (.zip)", "No", "Medium", "Legacy Vendor Feeds", "Requires custom parallel unpacking")
]

df_codecs = spark.createDataFrame(codecs, ["codec", "splittable", "compression_ratio", "primary_use_case", "notes"])
df_codecs.show(truncate=False)
notes: Compression formats without sync markers (GZIP, ZIP) are not splittable: a single 5GB GZIP file must be processed by exactly one Spark task. Bzip2 and Snappy (within container formats like Parquet/Avro) are splittable across tasks.
use_case: A regulatory agency deposits quarterly compliance archives as massive 5GB ZIP and TAR.GZ files. Standard Spark readers cannot split ZIP archives across executors, causing single-node driver OutOfMemory (OOM) crashes.

# 2. Once(): Single micro-batch. Dangerous if 100GB of backlogged data has accumulated.
# 3. AvailableNow(): Best practice for cost-effective incremental batching!
#    Processes backlog in multiple rate-limited micro-batches, commits checkpoints, and shuts down.

print("Streaming trigger architectural profiles defined.")

# --- Execution Step ---
import shutil
from pathlib import Path

stream_source_dir = Path("/tmp/stream_trigger_source_055")
stream_sink_dir = Path("/tmp/stream_trigger_sink_055")
stream_chk_dir = Path("/tmp/stream_trigger_chk_055")

for p in [stream_source_dir, stream_sink_dir, stream_chk_dir]:
    if p.exists():
        shutil.rmtree(p)
    p.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

# Write initial batch of files to source
with open(stream_source_dir / "events_1.json", "w") as f:
    f.write('{"id": 1, "val": "A"}\n{"id": 2, "val": "B"}\n')

schema = "id INT, val STRING"
df_file_stream = spark.readStream.schema(schema).json(str(stream_source_dir))

# Execute using Trigger.AvailableNow (terminates automatically when done)
query = (
    df_file_stream.writeStream
    .format("delta")
    .option("checkpointLocation", str(stream_chk_dir))
    .trigger(availableNow=True)
    .start(str(stream_sink_dir))
)

query.awaitTermination()
print("Trigger.AvailableNow completed successfully and terminated cleanly!")

print("Target Delta Table Output:")
spark.read.format("delta").load(str(stream_sink_dir)).show()

# --- Execution Step ---
# Add second batch of files
with open(stream_source_dir / "events_2.json", "w") as f:
    f.write('{"id": 3, "val": "C"}\n{"id": 4, "val": "D"}\n')

# Run second AvailableNow pass using the SAME checkpoint directory
query2 = (
    df_file_stream.writeStream
    .format("delta")
    .option("checkpointLocation", str(stream_chk_dir))
    .trigger(availableNow=True)
    .start(str(stream_sink_dir))
)
query2.awaitTermination()

While `Trigger.Once` loads all pending data into a single giant micro-batch (causing OutOfMemory crashes on large backlogs), `Trigger.AvailableNow` respects rate-limiting configurations, executing multiple properly-sized micro-batches until all backlogged data is processed, then cleanly terminates.

title: #056 Streaming Window Aggregations and Watermarking for Late-Arriving Events
description: Implement streaming window aggregations with watermarking: configure `withWatermark('event_time', '10 minutes')`, compute tumbling and sliding window metrics, and explain how the watermark dictates state eviction from RocksDB memory.
code:
import os
import sys
import shutil

# For local PySpark / CI execution, initialize a local session with Delta Lake support:

    spark

    from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
    spark = (
        SparkSession.builder
        .appName("UseCase_056_Streaming_Window_Aggregations_and_Watermarking_for_Late_Arriving_Events")
        .master("local[*]")
        .config("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "4")
        .config("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "true")
        .config("spark.sql.extensions", "io.delta.sql.DeltaSparkSessionExtension")
        .config("spark.sql.catalog.spark_catalog", "org.apache.spark.sql.delta.catalog.DeltaCatalog")
        .getOrCreate()
    )

from pyspark.sql import functions as F
from pyspark.sql import types as T
from pyspark.sql.window import Window

spark.sparkContext.setLogLevel("WARN")
print(f"Spark Version: {spark.version}")
print(f"Session Active: {spark.sparkContext.appName}")

# --- Execution Step ---
# Architectural Blueprint:
# Event Time: 12:00 -> Watermark = 12:00 - 10 min = 11:50
# Window [11:30 - 11:40]: Completely older than 11:50 -> State Evicted! No longer accepts updates.
# Window [11:45 - 11:55]: End time (11:55) > 11:50 -> Window still active in state memory.

print("Watermark state eviction semantics mapped.")

# --- Execution Step ---
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

base_time = datetime(2023, 11, 20, 12, 0, 0)

# Simulate events arriving out of chronological order
batch_events = [
    # On-time events
    (base_time, "Alice", 100),
    (base_time + timedelta(minutes=2), "Bob", 150),
    # Advance watermark to 12:15
    (base_time + timedelta(minutes=15), "Charlie", 300),
    # Late event from 12:03 (Arrives when max time is 12:15, delta = 12 min. Allowed if watermark >= 15 min!)
    (base_time + timedelta(minutes=3), "Alice", 50)
]

schema = "event_time TIMESTAMP, player STRING, score INT"
df_events = spark.createDataFrame(batch_events, schema)
df_events.show(truncate=False)

# --- Execution Step ---
# Tumbling window aggregation with watermark
df_windowed = (
    df_events
    .withWatermark("event_time", "15 minutes")
    .groupBy(
        F.window("event_time", "10 minutes"),
        "player"
    )
    .agg(
        F.sum("score").alias("total_score"),
        F.count("score").alias("events_count")
    )
    .select(
        "window.start",
        "window.end",
        "player",
        "total_score",
        "events_count"
    )
    .orderBy("start", "player")
)

print("Aggregated Window Output (Late Event Incorporated):")
df_windowed.show(truncate=False)
notes: A watermark specifies the maximum threshold by which event-time can lag behind the maximum event-time observed by the engine ($Watermark = Max(event\_time) - Delay$). Once a window's end time falls behind the watermark, Spark emits the final aggregate and purges the window's state from memory.
use_case: A mobile gaming platform aggregates player score events over 10-minute tumbling windows. Due to intermittent mobile connectivity and airplane mode, score events arrive up to 15 minutes late. The pipeline must incorporate late events without letting state size grow infinitely.

title: #058 Stream-Stream Dual Watermark Joins with Interval Conditions
description: Implement Stream-Stream joins in PySpark: configure dual watermarks on both streaming sides, specify mandatory time-range interval join constraints (`payment_time BETWEEN order_time AND order_time + INTERVAL 1 HOUR`), and explain how state retention boundaries are enforced.
code:
import os
import sys
import shutil
from pathlib import Path

# In Databricks, the SparkSession 'spark' is pre-initialized by the cluster.
# For local PySpark / CI execution, initialize a local session with Delta Lake support:
try:
    spark
except NameError:
    from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
    spark = (
        SparkSession.builder
        .appName("UseCase_058_Stream_Stream_Dual_Watermark_Joins_with_Interval_Conditions")
        .master("local[*]")
        .config("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "4")
        .config("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "true")
        .config("spark.sql.extensions", "io.delta.sql.DeltaSparkSessionExtension")
        .config("spark.sql.catalog.spark_catalog", "org.apache.spark.sql.delta.catalog.DeltaCatalog")
        .getOrCreate()
    )

from pyspark.sql import functions as F
from pyspark.sql import types as T
from pyspark.sql.window import Window

spark.sparkContext.setLogLevel("WARN")
print(f"Spark Version: {spark.version}")
print(f"Session Active: {spark.sparkContext.appName}")

# --- Execution Step ---
# Mandatory Requirements for Stream-Stream Joins:
# 1. Watermark defined on Stream 1: df_orders.withWatermark("order_time", "2 hours")
# 2. Watermark defined on Stream 2: df_payments.withWatermark("payment_time", "3 hours")
# 3. Time Interval Condition:
#    (orders.order_id == payments.order_id) &
#    (payments.payment_time >= orders.order_time) &
#    (payments.payment_time <= orders.order_time + expr("INTERVAL 1 HOUR"))

print("Stream-Stream state retention constraints blueprint mapped.")

# --- Execution Step ---
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

base_ts = datetime(2023, 11, 20, 10, 0, 0)

orders_batch = [
    ("ORD-1", 120.00, base_ts),
    ("ORD-2", 450.00, base_ts + timedelta(minutes=5)),
    ("ORD-3", 85.00,  base_ts + timedelta(minutes=10))
]

payments_batch = [
    ("ORD-1", "PAY-901", base_ts + timedelta(minutes=2)),   # Matched (2 min after order)
    ("ORD-2", "PAY-902", base_ts + timedelta(minutes=45)),  # Matched (45 min after order)
    ("ORD-99", "PAY-999", base_ts + timedelta(minutes=15))  # Unmatched payment
]

schema_ord = "order_id STRING, amount DOUBLE, order_time TIMESTAMP"
schema_pay = "order_id STRING, payment_id STRING, payment_time TIMESTAMP"

df_ord = spark.createDataFrame(orders_batch, schema_ord)
df_pay = spark.createDataFrame(payments_batch, schema_pay)

print("Orders Stream Batch:")
df_ord.show(truncate=False)
print("Payments Stream Batch:")
df_pay.show(truncate=False)

# --- Execution Step ---
# Join condition pairing primary key match with time range window
join_cond = (
    (df_ord["order_id"] == df_pay["order_id"]) &
    (df_pay["payment_time"] >= df_ord["order_time"]) &
    (df_pay["payment_time"] <= df_ord["order_time"] + F.expr("INTERVAL 1 HOUR"))
)

df_matched_orders = df_ord.join(df_pay, on=join_cond, how="inner").select(
    df_ord["order_id"],
    "amount",
    "order_time",
    "payment_id",
    "payment_time",
    F.round((F.col("payment_time").cast("long") - F.col("order_time").cast("long")) / 60.0, 1).alias("payment_delay_minutes")
)

print("Stream-Stream Matched Order-Payment Events:")
df_matched_orders.show(truncate=False)
notes: In a stream-stream join, both datasets are unbounded. Spark must buffer incoming rows from stream A in state store until a matching row arrives from stream B. To prevent state store memory from growing infinitely, Spark strictly requires both a watermark on each stream and a time interval constraint.
use_case: An online retail logistics platform matches checkout order events with payment confirmation events arriving from Stripe/PayPal across separate event streams. Orders and payments can arrive seconds or minutes apart.

description: Implement streaming deduplication: apply `withWatermark()` paired with `dropDuplicates()` on primary keys and event timestamps. Explain how the watermark bounds the historical key state maintained by the streaming engine.

from pyspark.sql import functions as F
from pyspark.sql import types as T
from pyspark.sql.window import Window

spark.sparkContext.setLogLevel("WARN")
print(f"Spark Version: {spark.version}")
print(f"Session Active: {spark.sparkContext.appName}")

# --- Execution Step ---
# Architectural Blueprint:
# stream.withWatermark("event_time", "20 minutes").dropDuplicates(["device_id", "event_time"])
# Keys older than (max_event_time - 20 minutes) are evicted from memory.
# New duplicates within the 20-minute window are safely identified and dropped!

print("Streaming deduplication memory bounds blueprint mapped.")

# --- Execution Step ---
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

base_ts = datetime(2023, 11, 20, 15, 0, 0)

telemetry_stream = [
    ("DEV-01", base_ts, 22.5),
    ("DEV-02", base_ts, 25.0),
    ("DEV-01", base_ts, 22.5), # Exact duplicate within window -> MUST DROP
    ("DEV-01", base_ts + timedelta(minutes=5), 23.0), # Valid new reading -> KEEP
    ("DEV-03", base_ts + timedelta(minutes=10), 19.5)
]

schema = "device_id STRING, event_time TIMESTAMP, temp DOUBLE"
df_stream_telemetry = spark.createDataFrame(telemetry_stream, schema)
df_stream_telemetry.show(truncate=False)

# --- Execution Step ---
# Deduplicate streaming data within a 20-minute watermark window
df_deduped = (
    df_stream_telemetry
    .withWatermark("event_time", "20 minutes")
    .dropDuplicates(["device_id", "event_time"])
)

print("Deduplicated Stream Output:")
df_deduped.orderBy("device_id", "event_time").show(truncate=False)

# Verification assertion
assert df_deduped.count() == 4, f"Expected 4 unique readings, found {df_deduped.count()}"
print("Streaming deduplication assertion verified successfully!")
notes: In Structured Streaming, calling `dropDuplicates(['key'])` without a watermark causes Spark to store every primary key ever seen in memory forever, eventually triggering an Executor OOM. Supplying a watermark allows Spark to evict keys older than the watermark threshold from the state store.
use_case: An IoT gateway ingests sensor readings from connected vehicles over cellular networks. When vehicles enter tunnels or experience network reconnects, duplicate messages are re-sent. The pipeline must eliminate duplicate sensor IDs within a rolling 20-minute window.

title: #060 Idempotent ACID Delta Upserts using writeStream.foreachBatch
description: Master `writeStream.foreachBatch()`: design a micro-batch function that executes an atomic `DeltaTable.merge()` operation, ensures idempotency across micro-batch retries, and avoids race conditions in distributed streaming sinks.
code:
import os
import sys
import shutil
from pathlib import Path

# In Databricks, the SparkSession 'spark' is pre-initialized by the cluster.
# For local PySpark / CI execution, initialize a local session with Delta Lake support:
try:
    spark
except NameError:
    from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
    spark = (
        SparkSession.builder
        .appName("UseCase_060_Idempotent_ACID_Delta_Upserts_using_writeStreamforeachBatch")
        .master("local[*]")
        .config("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "4")
        .config("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "true")
        .config("spark.sql.extensions", "io.delta.sql.DeltaSparkSessionExtension")
        .config("spark.sql.catalog.spark_catalog", "org.apache.spark.sql.delta.catalog.DeltaCatalog")
        .getOrCreate()
    )

from pyspark.sql import functions as F
from pyspark.sql import types as T
from pyspark.sql.window import Window

spark.sparkContext.setLogLevel("WARN")
print(f"Spark Version: {spark.version}")
print(f"Session Active: {spark.sparkContext.appName}")

# --- Execution Step ---
from delta.tables import DeltaTable

silver_ledger_path = "/tmp/delta_silver_ledger_060"
if Path(silver_ledger_path).exists():
    shutil.rmtree(silver_ledger_path)

initial_txns = [
    ("TXN-101", "CUST-1", 100.0, "PENDING", "2023-11-20 10:00:00"),
    ("TXN-102", "CUST-2", 250.0, "SETTLED", "2023-11-20 10:05:00")
]

schema = "txn_id STRING, customer_id STRING, amount DOUBLE, status STRING, updated_at STRING"
spark.createDataFrame(initial_txns, schema).write.format("delta").mode("overwrite").save(silver_ledger_path)

target_delta = DeltaTable.forPath(spark, silver_ledger_path)
print("Initial Silver Ledger Delta Table:")
target_delta.toDF().show()

# --- Execution Step ---
def upsert_to_delta(micro_batch_df, batch_id):
    """
    Invoked for each micro-batch. Performs idempotent MERGE into target Delta table.
    """
    print(f"--> Processing Micro-Batch ID: {batch_id} (Rows: {micro_batch_df.count()})")

    # 1. Deduplicate micro-batch by taking the latest update per txn_id
    window_spec = Window.partitionBy("txn_id").orderBy(F.col("updated_at").desc())
    deduped_batch = micro_batch_df.withColumn("rn", F.row_number().over(window_spec))                                 .filter(F.col("rn") == 1)                                 .drop("rn")

    # 2. Atomic MERGE into target Delta table
    target_table = DeltaTable.forPath(spark, silver_ledger_path)
    (
        target_table.alias("target")
        .merge(
            source=deduped_batch.alias("source"),
            condition="target.txn_id = source.txn_id"
        )
        .whenMatchedUpdate(
            set={
                "amount": F.col("source.amount"),
                "status": F.col("source.status"),
                "updated_at": F.col("source.updated_at")
            }
        )
        .whenNotMatchedInsertAll()
        .execute()
    )
    print(f"--> Micro-Batch {batch_id} merged successfully into Delta table.")

print("foreachBatch upsert function defined.")

# --- Execution Step ---
# Incoming micro-batch: TXN-101 is updated from PENDING to SETTLED; TXN-103 is a new transaction
micro_batch_1 = [
    ("TXN-101", "CUST-1", 100.0, "SETTLED", "2023-11-20 10:15:00"), # Update
    ("TXN-103", "CUST-3", 75.0,  "SETTLED", "2023-11-20 10:20:00")  # Insert
]

df_mb1 = spark.createDataFrame(micro_batch_1, schema)

# Execute the upsert function directly (simulating writeStream.foreachBatch)
upsert_to_delta(df_mb1, batch_id=1)

print("Final Target Delta Table (Notice TXN-101 updated, TXN-103 inserted):")
target_delta.toDF().orderBy("txn_id").show()
notes: `foreachBatch` gives access to the output DataFrame of each micro-batch as a standard static DataFrame. This allows executing non-streaming operations—such as Delta Lake `MERGE INTO`, writing to multiple destinations, or executing custom API calls—inside a streaming query.
use_case: A payments streaming pipeline consumes live financial transactions that include both new purchases and refund updates to existing transactions. Standard streaming `append` creates duplicate rows; the stream must perform idempotent ACID `MERGE INTO` operations into target Delta tables.

description: Master arbitrary stateful streaming concepts: compare simple window aggregations with custom state machines, understand the mechanics of `mapGroupsWithState` and `flatMapGroupsWithState`, manage state expiration timeouts (ProcessingTime vs EventTime), and handle state state eviction.
code:
import os
import sys
import shutil
from pathlib import Path

try:

    from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
    spark = (
        SparkSession.builder
        .appName("UseCase_061_Arbitrary_Stateful_Streaming_Operations_with_FlatMapGroupsWithState_Concepts")
        .master("local[*]")
        .config("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "4")
        .config("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "true")
        .config("spark.sql.extensions", "io.delta.sql.DeltaSparkSessionExtension")
        .config("spark.sql.catalog.spark_catalog", "org.apache.spark.sql.delta.catalog.DeltaCatalog")
        .getOrCreate()
    )

from pyspark.sql import functions as F
from pyspark.sql import types as T
from pyspark.sql.window import Window

spark.sparkContext.setLogLevel("WARN")
print(f"Spark Version: {spark.version}")
print(f"Session Active: {spark.sparkContext.appName}")

# --- Execution Step ---
# State Machine Model:
# Inputs: (Key: user_id, Value: current_cell_event, State: UserTravelHistory)
# Operations:
# 1. If State is Empty: Initialize state with current tower and timestamp.
# 2. If State Exists: Calculate speed/distance from last tower.
# 3. If impossible velocity detected (> 500 mph): Emit FRAUD_ALERT event!
# 4. Update state with current tower.
# 5. Set Timeout: Evict state after 30 minutes of inactivity to bound RocksDB memory.

print("Arbitrary state machine architecture mapped.")

# --- Execution Step ---
tower_events = [
    ("USER-1", "TOWER-NYC", 40.7128, -74.0060, "2023-11-20 10:00:00"),
    ("USER-1", "TOWER-BOS", 42.3601, -71.0589, "2023-11-20 10:08:00"), # 200 miles in 8 min -> Impossible speed!
    ("USER-2", "TOWER-SFO", 37.7749, -122.4194, "2023-11-20 10:00:00"),
    ("USER-2", "TOWER-OAK", 37.8044, -122.2712, "2023-11-20 10:30:00") # 10 miles in 30 min -> Normal
]

schema = "user_id STRING, tower_id STRING, lat DOUBLE, lon DOUBLE, event_time STRING"
df_towers = spark.createDataFrame(tower_events, schema).withColumn("ts", F.to_timestamp("event_time"))

# Stateful calculation: compare with previous tower event in state
user_state_win = Window.partitionBy("user_id").orderBy("ts")

df_state_transitions = (
    df_towers
    .withColumn("prev_tower", F.lag("tower_id").over(user_state_win))
    .withColumn("prev_lat", F.lag("lat").over(user_state_win))
    .withColumn("prev_lon", F.lag("lon").over(user_state_win))
    .withColumn("prev_ts", F.lag("ts").over(user_state_win))
    .withColumn(
        "elapsed_minutes",
        (F.col("ts").cast("long") - F.col("prev_ts").cast("long")) / 60.0
    )
    .withColumn(
        # Approximate distance in miles
        "distance_miles",
        F.round(F.sqrt(F.pow((F.col("lat") - F.col("prev_lat")) * 69.0, 2) + F.pow((F.col("lon") - F.col("prev_lon")) * 55.0, 2)), 1)
    )
    .withColumn(
        "calculated_mph",
        F.when(F.col("elapsed_minutes") > 0, F.round(F.col("distance_miles") / (F.col("elapsed_minutes") / 60.0), 1)).otherwise(0.0)
    )
    .withColumn(
        "is_fraud_velocity",
        F.when(F.col("calculated_mph") > 500.0, True).otherwise(False)
    )
)

print("Stateful Machine Velocity Analysis:")
df_state_transitions.select("user_id", "tower_id", "prev_tower", "elapsed_minutes", "distance_miles", "calculated_mph", "is_fraud_velocity").show(truncate=False)

# --- Execution Step ---
# Production Timeout Guidelines:
# 1. EventTimeTimeout: State expires based on the watermark timestamp (reproducible across replays).
# 2. ProcessingTimeTimeout: State expires based on wall-clock time (simpler, but non-deterministic in replays).
# Always call state.remove() upon session termination to reclaim RocksDB memory!

print("State timeout and memory cleanup rules verified.")
notes: `mapGroupsWithState` and `flatMapGroupsWithState` allow developers to maintain arbitrary user-defined state objects across streaming batches. While full API implementation requires Scala/Java or PySpark with custom encoders, understanding the stateful machine model is critical for senior data engineers.
use_case: A telecommunications security monitor detects SIM-swap and fraud patterns across customer cell towers. A fraud flag must trigger only if a user connects to two distinct cell towers separated by 500+ miles within a 15-minute window.

from pyspark.sql import functions as F
from pyspark.sql import types as T
from pyspark.sql.window import Window

spark.sparkContext.setLogLevel("WARN")
print(f"Spark Version: {spark.version}")
print(f"Session Active: {spark.sparkContext.appName}")

# --- Execution Step ---
from pyspark.sql.streaming import StreamingQueryListener

class PipelineSLAListener(StreamingQueryListener):
    def onQueryStarted(self, event):
        print(f"[OBSERVABILITY] Query Started! ID: {event.id} | Name: {event.name}")

    def onQueryProgress(self, event):
        progress = event.progress
        batch_id = progress.batchId
        input_rate = progress.inputRowsPerSecond
        proc_rate = progress.processedRowsPerSecond
        num_input = progress.numInputRows

        # Check if processing rate lags behind input rate (Backlog accumulation!)
        status = "HEALTHY"
        if input_rate > 0 and proc_rate < (input_rate * 0.8):
            status = "WARNING: PROCESSING_LAG_DETECTED"

        print(f"[METRIC] Batch: {batch_id} | In: {num_input} rows | InRate: {input_rate:.1f}/s | ProcRate: {proc_rate:.1f}/s | {status}")

    def onQueryTerminated(self, event):
        if event.exception:
            print(f"[ALERT] Query CRASHED with error: {event.exception}")
        else:
            print("[OBSERVABILITY] Query Terminated cleanly.")

print("PipelineSLAListener class defined.")

# --- Execution Step ---
# Register the listener
sla_listener = PipelineSLAListener()
spark.streams.addListener(sla_listener)
print("StreamingQueryListener registered with SparkSession.")

# --- Execution Step ---
import time

df_rate = spark.readStream.format("rate").option("rowsPerSecond", 10).load()

q_monitored = (
    df_rate.writeStream
    .format("memory")
    .queryName("sla_telemetry_demo")
    .start()
)

# Let run for 2.5 seconds to trigger progress callbacks
time.sleep(2.5)

q_monitored.stop()
print("Monitored query completed.")
notes: Spark's `StreamingQueryListener` provides an asynchronous callback API. When registered with `spark.streams.addListener()`, it captures event telemetry for all queries running in the SparkSession without introducing runtime overhead into the data processing tasks.
use_case: An enterprise fintech streaming pipeline must maintain an SLA of processing events within 60 seconds of origination. If a backlog builds up or micro-batch processing time spikes, on-call engineers must be alerted before SLA violations occur.

Contrast deterministic replayability, performance, and storage footprint.

import os
import sys

        SparkSession.builder
        .appName("UseCase_067_Distributed_Surrogate_Key_Generation_monotonically_increasing_id_vs_xxhash64_vs_UUIDs")
        .master("local[*]")
        .config("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "4")
        .config("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "true")
        .config("spark.sql.extensions", "io.delta.sql.DeltaSparkSessionExtension")
        .config("spark.sql.catalog.spark_catalog", "org.apache.spark.sql.delta.catalog.DeltaCatalog")
        .getOrCreate()
    )

from pyspark.sql import functions as F
from pyspark.sql import types as T
from pyspark.sql.window import Window

spark.sparkContext.setLogLevel("WARN")
print(f"Spark Version: {spark.version}")
print(f"Session Active: {spark.sparkContext.appName}")

# --- Execution Step ---
natural_customers = [
    ("NAT-1001", "Alice Smith", "2023-01-10"),
    ("NAT-1002", "Bob Jones", "2023-02-15"),
    ("NAT-1003", "Charlie Day", "2023-03-20"),
    ("NAT-1004", "Diana Prince", "2023-04-25")
]

schema = "natural_key STRING, name STRING, created_at STRING"
df_cust = spark.createDataFrame(natural_customers, schema).repartition(2)
print(f"Partitions: {df_cust.rdd.getNumPartitions()}")

# --- Execution Step ---
df_keys = (
    df_cust
    # 1. Monotonically increasing ID (Fast, non-contiguous, partition-dependent)
    .withColumn("surrogate_monotonic_id", F.monotonically_increasing_id())
    # 2. Deterministic 64-bit integer hash (Replayable, 100% deterministic, 8 bytes)
    .withColumn("surrogate_xxhash64", F.xxhash64(F.col("natural_key"), F.col("created_at")))
    # 3. MD5/SHA256 string hash (Deterministic, 32/64 character string, higher storage cost)
    .withColumn("surrogate_sha256", F.sha2(F.col("natural_key"), 256))
    # 4. Random UUID (Unique, non-deterministic across pipeline reruns)
    .withColumn("surrogate_uuid", F.expr("uuid()"))
)

df_keys.select("natural_key", "surrogate_monotonic_id", "surrogate_xxhash64", "surrogate_uuid").show(truncate=False)

# --- Execution Step ---
# Re-evaluating xxhash64 on the same inputs yields identical hash values
df_recheck = df_cust.withColumn("recheck_hash", F.xxhash64(F.col("natural_key"), F.col("created_at")))
diff_count = df_keys.join(df_recheck, on="natural_key").filter(F.col("surrogate_xxhash64") != F.col("recheck_hash")).count()

assert diff_count == 0, "Deterministic hash mismatch detected!"
print("xxhash64 verified as 100% deterministic across distributed runs!")
notes: `monotonically_increasing_id()` generates 64-bit integers where the upper 33 bits represent the partition ID and the lower 31 bits represent the row ID within the partition. While fast, IDs are NOT contiguous and change if the partition count changes. `xxhash64(concat_ws())` produces deterministic 64-bit hash keys that remain identical across pipeline replays.
use_case: A lakehouse dimensional model builds customer and account dimension tables. Business analysts require synthetic integer or hash surrogate keys to decouple dimensional records from operational natural keys and enable SCD Type 2 version tracking.

title: #069 Slowly Changing Dimension Type 2 (SCD Type 2) Historical Tracking with Effective Dates
category: Lakehouse Data Modeling, CDC & SCD Implementation
description: Implement Slowly Changing Dimension Type 2 (SCD Type 2) in PySpark: maintain `effective_start_date`, `effective_end_date`, and `is_current` active flag columns. When an attribute changes, expire the current record by setting `effective_end_date` and insert a new active record.
code:
import os
import sys
import shutil
from pathlib import Path

# In Databricks, the SparkSession 'spark' is pre-initialized by the cluster.
# For local PySpark / CI execution, initialize a local session with Delta Lake support:
try:
    spark
except NameError:
    from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
    spark = (
        SparkSession.builder
        .appName("UseCase_069_Slowly_Changing_Dimension_Type_2_SCD_Type_2_Historical_Tracking_with_Effective_Dates")
        .master("local[*]")
        .config("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "4")
        .config("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "true")
        .config("spark.sql.extensions", "io.delta.sql.DeltaSparkSessionExtension")
        .config("spark.sql.catalog.spark_catalog", "org.apache.spark.sql.delta.catalog.DeltaCatalog")
        .getOrCreate()
    )

from pyspark.sql import functions as F
from pyspark.sql import types as T
from pyspark.sql.window import Window

spark.sparkContext.setLogLevel("WARN")
print(f"Spark Version: {spark.version}")
print(f"Session Active: {spark.sparkContext.appName}")

# --- Execution Step ---
from delta.tables import DeltaTable

scd2_path = "/tmp/delta_dim_customer_scd2_069"
if Path(scd2_path).exists():
    shutil.rmtree(scd2_path)

initial_scd2 = [
    (1, "C-101", "Alice", "Austin", "2023-01-01", "9999-12-31", True),
    (2, "C-102", "Bob", "Seattle", "2023-01-01", "9999-12-31", True)
]

schema = "sk_id LONG, cust_id STRING, name STRING, city STRING, start_date STRING, end_date STRING, is_current BOOLEAN"
spark.createDataFrame(initial_scd2, schema).write.format("delta").mode("overwrite").save(scd2_path)

dt_scd2 = DeltaTable.forPath(spark, scd2_path)
print("Initial Active SCD Type 2 Dimension:")
dt_scd2.toDF().show()

# --- Execution Step ---
new_cdc_feed = [
    ("C-101", "Alice", "Denver", "2023-11-20")
]

df_incoming = spark.createDataFrame(new_cdc_feed, ["cust_id", "name", "city", "change_date"])
df_incoming.show()

# --- Execution Step ---
# Step 1: Identify existing records that need expiration
df_current = dt_scd2.toDF().filter(F.col("is_current") == True)

df_to_expire = df_incoming.join(
    df_current,
    (df_incoming["cust_id"] == df_current["cust_id"]) & (df_incoming["city"] != df_current["city"]),
    how="inner"
).select(df_current["sk_id"], df_incoming["change_date"])

# Expire old records: set end_date and is_current = False
for row in df_to_expire.collect():
    dt_scd2.update(
        condition=F.col("sk_id") == row.sk_id,
        set={"end_date": F.lit(row.change_date), "is_current": F.lit(False)}
    )

# Step 2: Insert new active record
max_sk = dt_scd2.toDF().agg(F.max("sk_id")).first()[0] or 0

df_new_inserts = df_incoming.select(
    (F.lit(max_sk) + F.monotonically_increasing_id() + 1).alias("sk_id"),
    "cust_id",
    "name",
    "city",
    F.col("change_date").alias("start_date"),
    F.lit("9999-12-31").alias("end_date"),
    F.lit(True).alias("is_current")
)

df_new_inserts.write.format("delta").mode("append").save(scd2_path)

print("Final SCD Type 2 Dimension Table (Notice Alice's historical record preserved!):")
dt_scd2.toDF().orderBy("cust_id", "start_date").show()
notes: SCD Type 2 preserves the full history of attribute changes over time. description: Ingest and process Debezium CDC streams in PySpark: parse the nested JSON envelope, handle out-of-order CDC events using sequence numbers/timestamps, execute conditional MERGE into target Delta tables, and handle hard deletes gracefully.
code:
import os
import sys
import shutil
from pathlib import Path

        SparkSession.builder

        .master("local[*]")
        .config("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "4")
        .config("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "true")
        .config("spark.sql.extensions", "io.delta.sql.DeltaSparkSessionExtension")
        .config("spark.sql.catalog.spark_catalog", "org.apache.spark.sql.delta.catalog.DeltaCatalog")
        .getOrCreate()
    )

from pyspark.sql import functions as F
from pyspark.sql import types as T
from pyspark.sql.window import Window

spark.sparkContext.setLogLevel("WARN")
print(f"Spark Version: {spark.version}")
print(f"Session Active: {spark.sparkContext.appName}")

# --- Execution Step ---
cdc_raw_events = [
    # Insert SKU-101
    ('{"before": null, "after": {"sku": "SKU-101", "stock": 100, "price": 20.0}, "op": "c", "ts_ms": 1700560000}'),
    # Update SKU-101 stock to 80
    ('{"before": {"sku": "SKU-101", "stock": 100, "price": 20.0}, "after": {"sku": "SKU-101", "stock": 80, "price": 20.0}, "op": "u", "ts_ms": 1700560500}'),
    # Insert SKU-102
    ('{"before": null, "after": {"sku": "SKU-102", "stock": 50, "price": 45.0}, "op": "c", "ts_ms": 1700560100}'),
    # Delete SKU-102
    ('{"before": {"sku": "SKU-102", "stock": 50, "price": 45.0}, "after": null, "op": "d", "ts_ms": 1700560800}')
]

rdd_cdc = spark.sparkContext.parallelize(cdc_raw_events)
df_raw_cdc = spark.read.json(rdd_cdc)
df_raw_cdc.printSchema()
df_raw_cdc.show(truncate=False)

# --- Execution Step ---
# Extract target attributes from after struct (or before struct for deletes)
df_flattened_cdc = df_raw_cdc.select(
    F.coalesce(F.col("after.sku"), F.col("before.sku")).alias("sku"),
    F.col("after.stock").alias("stock"),
    F.col("after.price").alias("price"),
    F.col("op"),
    F.col("ts_ms")
)

# Deduplicate to find the latest operation per SKU
win_latest = Window.partitionBy("sku").orderBy(F.col("ts_ms").desc())
df_latest_cdc = (
    df_flattened_cdc
    .withColumn("rn", F.row_number().over(win_latest))
    .filter(F.col("rn") == 1)
    .drop("rn")
)

print("Deduplicated Latest CDC State:")
df_latest_cdc.show()

# --- Execution Step ---
from delta.tables import DeltaTable

delta_cdc_target = "/tmp/delta_inventory_cdc_071"
if Path(delta_cdc_target).exists():
    shutil.rmtree(delta_cdc_target)

# Initialize target table
init_schema = "sku STRING, stock INT, price DOUBLE, last_ts LONG"
spark.createDataFrame([], init_schema).write.format("delta").mode("overwrite").save(delta_cdc_target)

target_tbl = DeltaTable.forPath(spark, delta_cdc_target)

(
    target_tbl.alias("target")
    .merge(
        source=df_latest_cdc.alias("source"),
        condition="target.sku = source.sku"
    )
    .whenMatchedDelete(
        condition="source.op = 'd'"
    )
    .whenMatchedUpdate(
        set={"stock": F.col("source.stock"), "price": F.col("source.price"), "last_ts": F.col("source.ts_ms")}
    )
    .whenNotMatchedInsert(
        condition="source.op != 'd'",
        values={"sku": F.col("source.sku"), "stock": F.col("source.stock"), "price": F.col("source.price"), "last_ts": F.col("source.ts_ms")}
    )
    .execute()
)

print("Target Delta Inventory Table after CDC Replay (SKU-101 updated, SKU-102 deleted):")
target_tbl.toDF().show()
notes: Debezium CDC events contain metadata fields: `op` (operation: c=create, u=update, d=delete, r=snapshot read) and `ts_ms` (source commit timestamp). Applying CDC records requires deduplicating within each micro-batch by taking the latest `ts_ms` before merging.
use_case: A transactional MySQL inventory database streams row-level changes into Kafka via Debezium CDC. Debezium publishes events containing `before`, `after`, and `op` flags (`c` for create, `u` for update, `d` for delete). The lakehouse must reconstruct current database state.

# Small customer dimension table
cust_dim = [("HOT_KEY", "Guest Shopper"), ("CUST_001", "Regular Shopper")]
df_dim = spark.createDataFrame(cust_dim, ["customer_id", "profile"])

# Replicate dimension keys across all possible salt values [0, 1, 2, 3]
df_dim_exploded = (
    df_dim
    .withColumn("salt_array", F.array([F.lit(i) for i in range(SALT_FACTOR)]))
    .select("customer_id", "profile", F.explode("salt_array").alias("salt"))
    .withColumn("salted_key", F.concat(F.col("customer_id"), F.lit("_SALT_"), F.col("salt")))
)

# Execute join on salted_key
df_balanced_join = df_salted.join(df_dim_exploded, on="salted_key", how="inner")

print("Post-Join Partition Distribution (Notice even distribution across partitions):")
df_balanced_join.withColumn("pid", F.spark_partition_id()).groupBy("pid").count().orderBy("pid").show()
notes: Data skew occurs when one partition contains disproportionately more records than others. In SortMergeJoin, rows with identical keys hash to the same reducer task. Salting appends a random salt $0 \dots (K-1)$ to the skewed key, distributing the single hot key evenly across $K$ reducer partitions.
use_case: A national e-commerce platform joins website clicks with user accounts. Out of 100 million clicks, 40% belong to guest user ID `GUEST_000` (null/anonymous user). The join stalls at 99% for 45 minutes because a single executor task processes all 40 million guest clicks, causing shuffle spill and OOM.

print(f"Session Active: {spark.sparkContext.appName}")

# --- Execution Step ---
# Tuning Formula:
# Target Partition Size = 100MB to 200MB
# Shuffle Partitions = Total Input Data at Shuffle / 150MB
# Example: 10GB dataset -> 10,000MB / 150MB ≈ 67 partitions
# Example: 500GB dataset -> 500,000MB / 150MB ≈ 3,333 partitions

df_small = spark.range(1, 50000, 1, 4).withColumn("group", F.col("id") % 10)

t_default = time.time() - t0
print(f"200 Partitions Execution Time: {t_default:.3f}s (High task scheduling overhead)")

# Run with tuned 4 shuffle partitions
spark.conf.set("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "4")
t0 = time.time()
c2 = df_small.groupBy("group").count().collect()
t_tuned = time.time() - t0
print(f"4 Partitions Execution Time: {t_tuned:.3f}s (Speedup: {t_default/max(t_tuned, 0.001):.1f}x)")

# --- Execution Step ---

spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "true")
spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.advisoryPartitionSizeInBytes", str(64 * 1024 * 1024)) # 64MB advisory size

If too low, partition data exceeds executor RAM, triggering costly disk spills or OOM errors. Rule of thumb: $ShufflePartitions = ShuffleDataSize / 150MB$.

title: #085 Fixing Accidental Cartesian Products and BroadcastNestedLoopJoins
category: Performance Tuning, Query Optimization & Skew Mitigation
description: Detect and fix accidental Cartesian products: identify `BroadcastNestedLoopJoin` and `CartesianProduct` operators in execution plans, understand why non-equi joins and OR join conditions disable hash joins, and rewrite queries using UNIONs or window functions.
code:

        SparkSession.builder

        .master("local[*]")
        .config("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "4")
        .config("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "true")
        .config("spark.sql.extensions", "io.delta.sql.DeltaSparkSessionExtension")
        .config("spark.sql.catalog.spark_catalog", "org.apache.spark.sql.delta.catalog.DeltaCatalog")
        .getOrCreate()
    )

from pyspark.sql import functions as F
from pyspark.sql import types as T
from pyspark.sql.window import Window

spark.sparkContext.setLogLevel("WARN")
print(f"Spark Version: {spark.version}")
print(f"Session Active: {spark.sparkContext.appName}")

# --- Execution Step ---
df1 = spark.createDataFrame([(1, "alice@a.com"), (2, "bob@b.com")], ["id", "email"])
df2 = spark.createDataFrame([(1, "alice@work.com"), (3, "bob@b.com")], ["id", "email"])

# Dangerous Join: Joining with OR condition disables Hash Join!
dangerous_join = df1.join(df2, (df1["id"] == df2["id"]) | (df1["email"] == df2["email"]), how="inner")

print("=== DANGEROUS PHYSICAL PLAN (Notice BroadcastNestedLoopJoin or CartesianProduct!) ===")
dangerous_join.explain(mode="simple")

# --- Execution Step ---
# Optimized Architecture: Split OR condition into two separate Equi-Joins and Union
# 1. Match on ID (fast HashJoin)
df_match_id = df1.join(df2, on="id", how="inner").select(df1["id"], df1["email"])

# 2. Match on Email (fast HashJoin)
df_match_email = df1.join(df2, on="email", how="inner").select(df1["id"], df1["email"])

# 3. Combine with distinct to deduplicate matches
df_optimized = df_match_id.unionByName(df_match_email).distinct()

print("=== OPTIMIZED PHYSICAL PLAN (Both branches use high-speed Hash Joins!) ===")
df_optimized.explain(mode="simple")
df_optimized.show()

# --- Execution Step ---
print("Both implementations produce identical business results, but the optimized query scales linearly O(N) instead of quadratically O(N*M)!")
notes: SortMergeJoin and BroadcastHashJoin strictly require equi-join conditions (`=`). When a join predicate contains an `OR`, `<>`, or non-equi condition without an equality key, Spark must fall back to a Cartesian Product (complexity $O(N 	imes M)$), generating quadratic row comparisons.
use_case: A junior engineer submits a join query where the join condition accidentally uses an OR operator across two conditions: `ON (a.id = b.id OR a.email = b.email)`. The job hangs indefinitely because Catalyst cannot use hash joins or sort-merge joins, falling back to a catastrophic Cartesian product.

]

            env_var = f"{scope.upper()}_{key.upper()}"

category: Databricks Platform, Unity Catalog, Security & FinOps
description: Master Delta Live Tables (DLT) & Lakeflow Declarative Pipelines: understand the `@dlt.table` and `@dlt.view` decorators, compare the 3 expectation types (`expect`, `expect_or_drop`, `expect_or_fail`), configure streaming tables vs materialized views, and inspect pipeline event logs.

        .getOrCreate()

from pyspark.sql import functions as F
from pyspark.sql import types as T
from pyspark.sql.window import Window

print(f"Spark Version: {spark.version}")
print(f"Session Active: {spark.sparkContext.appName}")

# --- Execution Step ---
# Production Delta Live Tables / Lakeflow Pipeline:
dlt_pipeline_code = """
import dlt
from pyspark.sql import functions as F

# 1. Bronze Streaming Table (Raw Ingestion)
@dlt.table(
    comment="Raw streaming invoices ingested via Auto Loader",
    table_properties={"quality": "bronze"}
)
def invoices_raw():
    return (
        spark.readStream.format("cloudFiles")
        .option("cloudFiles.format", "json")
        .load("/Volumes/enterprise/raw/invoices/")
    )

# 2. Silver Table with Data Quality Expectations
@dlt.table(
    comment="Cleansed invoices with data quality rules"
)
@dlt.expect("valid_invoice_no", "invoice_no IS NOT NULL")
@dlt.expect_or_drop("valid_positive_amount", "amount > 0")
@dlt.expect_or_fail("valid_status", "status IN ('APPROVED', 'PENDING', 'REJECTED')")
def invoices_silver():
    return dlt.read_stream("invoices_raw").select("invoice_no", "amount", "status")

# 3. Gold Materialized View (Business Summary)
@dlt.table(
    comment="Daily aggregated sales summary"
)
def invoices_gold():
    return (
        dlt.read("invoices_silver")
        .groupBy("status")
        .agg(F.sum("amount").alias("total_amount"))
    )
"""

print("Lakeflow / DLT Declarative Pipeline Blueprint defined:")
print(dlt_pipeline_code)

# --- Execution Step ---
# Mock incoming data with varying levels of quality issues
raw_batch = [
    ("INV-01", 100.0, "APPROVED"),   # Valid
    ("INV-02", -50.0, "APPROVED"),   # Violates positive amount -> DROP
    (None,     250.0, "PENDING"),    # Violates non-null -> LOG (retain row)
    ("INV-03", 500.0, "INVALID_STATE")# Violates valid_status -> FAIL PIPELINE
]

schema = "invoice_no STRING, amount DOUBLE, status STRING"
df_test = spark.createDataFrame(raw_batch, schema)

# Behavior 1: expect_or_drop (Filters out violating rows)
df_clean = df_test.filter(F.col("amount") > 0)
print(f"After expect_or_drop (amount > 0): {df_clean.count()} rows retained.")
df_clean.show()

# Behavior 2: expect_or_fail (Throws exception if any row violates rule)
has_fatal_error = df_clean.filter(~F.col("status").isin(["APPROVED", "PENDING", "REJECTED"])).count() > 0
if has_fatal_error:
    print("ALERT: expect_or_fail triggered! Pipeline run aborted due to invalid status values.")

# --- Execution Step ---
exp_modes = [
    ("@dlt.expect('rule', 'condition')", "Logs violation count to event log; retains row in table."),
    ("@dlt.expect_or_drop('rule', 'condition')", "Logs violation; automatically drops invalid rows from target table."),
    ("@dlt.expect_or_fail('rule', 'condition')", "Logs violation; immediately aborts pipeline execution with error.")
]

for mode, behavior in exp_modes:
    print(f" {mode}\n   -> {behavior}")
notes: Lakeflow Declarative Pipelines (DLT) allow data engineers to define *what* tables to produce rather than *how* to orchestrate them. DLT automatically constructs the DAG, provisions clusters, manages checkpoints, and captures data quality metrics per expectation rule.
use_case: An enterprise financial lakehouse migrates manual notebook pipelines to Databricks Lakeflow Declarative Pipelines (Delta Live Tables). The platform requires declarative Medallion pipelines with embedded Data Quality Expectations that log, drop, or fail on bad data.

description: Build an end-to-end financial data engineering project: (1) Ingest raw swipes into Bronze Delta table with audit columns, (2) Cleanse, parse timestamps, and join against customer profiles in Silver, (3) Apply window-based fraud detection rules (swipes within 2 minutes in different cities), and (4) Publish a Gold Customer 360 Risk Summary table.

import os
import sys
import shutil
from pathlib import Path

# In Databricks, the SparkSession 'spark' is pre-initialized by the cluster.

    spark

        SparkSession.builder

        .master("local[*]")
        .config("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "4")
        .config("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "true")
        .config("spark.sql.extensions", "io.delta.sql.DeltaSparkSessionExtension")
        .config("spark.sql.catalog.spark_catalog", "org.apache.spark.sql.delta.catalog.DeltaCatalog")
        .getOrCreate()
    )

from pyspark.sql import functions as F
from pyspark.sql import types as T
from pyspark.sql.window import Window

spark.sparkContext.setLogLevel("WARN")
print(f"Spark Version: {spark.version}")
print(f"Session Active: {spark.sparkContext.appName}")

# --- Execution Step ---
bronze_fraud_path = "/tmp/project_finance_bronze_096"
if Path(bronze_fraud_path).exists():
    shutil.rmtree(bronze_fraud_path)

raw_swipes = [
    ("SW-01", "CARD-101", 85.50,  "New York", "2023-11-20 12:00:00"),
    ("SW-02", "CARD-101", 1200.00,"London",   "2023-11-20 12:05:00"), # 5 min later in London -> FRAUD!
    ("SW-03", "CARD-102", 45.00,  "Chicago",  "2023-11-20 12:00:00"),
    ("SW-04", "CARD-102", 52.00,  "Chicago",  "2023-11-20 12:45:00"),
    ("SW-05", "CARD-103", 9500.00,"Miami",    "2023-11-20 12:10:00")  # Huge transaction
]

schema = "swipe_id STRING, card_id STRING, amount DOUBLE, city STRING, swipe_time STRING"
df_bronze_swipes = spark.createDataFrame(raw_swipes, schema).withColumn("_ingested_at", F.current_timestamp())

df_bronze_swipes.write.format("delta").mode("append").save(bronze_fraud_path)
print("Step 1 Complete: Raw card swipes landed in Bronze Delta table.")

# --- Execution Step ---
df_bronze = spark.read.format("delta").load(bronze_fraud_path).withColumn("ts", F.to_timestamp("swipe_time"))

card_window = Window.partitionBy("card_id").orderBy("ts")

df_silver_fraud = (
    df_bronze
    .withColumn("prev_city", F.lag("city").over(card_window))
    .withColumn("prev_ts", F.lag("ts").over(card_window))
    .withColumn("elapsed_minutes", (F.col("ts").cast("long") - F.col("prev_ts").cast("long")) / 60.0)
    .withColumn(
        "is_geo_velocity_fraud",
        F.when(
            (F.col("prev_city").isNotNull()) &
            (F.col("city") != F.col("prev_city")) &
            (F.col("elapsed_minutes") < 30.0),
            True
        ).otherwise(False)
    )
    .withColumn(
        "is_high_value_alert",
        F.when(F.col("amount") >= 5000.0, True).otherwise(False)
    )
    .withColumn(
        "fraud_risk_score",
        F.when(F.col("is_geo_velocity_fraud"), 95)
         .when(F.col("is_high_value_alert"), 75)
         .otherwise(10)
    )
)

print("Step 2 Complete: Silver Cleansed Swipes with Fraud Risk Scores:")
df_silver_fraud.select("swipe_id", "card_id", "amount", "city", "prev_city", "elapsed_minutes", "fraud_risk_score").show()

# --- Execution Step ---
df_gold_card360 = (
    df_silver_fraud
    .groupBy("card_id")
    .agg(
        F.count("swipe_id").alias("total_swipes"),
        F.round(F.sum("amount"), 2).alias("total_spend"),
        F.max("fraud_risk_score").alias("peak_risk_score"),
        F.sum(F.when(F.col("fraud_risk_score") >= 75, 1).otherwise(0)).alias("suspicious_events_count")
    )
    .withColumn(
        "account_status",
        F.when(F.col("peak_risk_score") >= 90, "LOCKED_FRAUD_HOLD")
         .when(F.col("peak_risk_score") >= 70, "FLAGGED_FOR_REVIEW")
         .otherwise("GOOD_STANDING")
    )
)

print("Step 3 Complete: Gold Customer 360 Risk Scorecard:")
df_gold_card360.show()
notes: Financial fraud detection requires low latency and high consistency. Combining Delta Lake ACID guarantees with window-based temporal heuristics allows detecting impossible geographic travel velocities and abnormal spend spikes without complex external ML infrastructure.
use_case: A tier-1 retail bank processes 50 million credit card swipe transactions daily. Risk engineering must build an end-to-end Medallion pipeline that ingests raw swipes, calculates real-time risk scores (geographical velocity, transaction spikes > 3x average, rapid successive swipes within 2 minutes), and flags fraudulent transactions for real-time card blocking.

raw_patients = [

]

df_raw_ehr.show()

# --- Execution Step ---
SECRET_SALT = "CLINICAL_SALT_KEY_99"

df_deidentified = (
    df_raw_ehr
    # 1. Pseudonymize MRN using salted SHA-256 hash
    .withColumn("research_patient_id", F.substring(F.sha2(F.concat(F.col("mrn"), F.lit(SECRET_SALT)), 256), 1, 16))
    # 2. Drop direct name entirely
    .drop("name", "mrn")
    # 3. Truncate ZIP code to first 3 digits
    .withColumn("zip3", F.substring(F.col("zip_code"), 1, 3))
    .drop("zip_code")
    # 4. Calculate patient age instead of revealing full DOB
    .withColumn("patient_age", F.floor(F.datediff(F.current_date(), F.to_date("dob")) / 365.25))
    .drop("dob")
)

    .withColumn("admit", F.to_timestamp("admit_ts"))

)

print("HIPAA-Compliant De-Identified Research Table (Safe for ML & Clinical Trials):")

daily_usage = [
    ("SUB-1", "2023-11-01", 1.5, 45, 0),
    ("SUB-1", "2023-11-05", 2.0, 30, 0),
    ("SUB-1", "2023-11-15", 0.5, 10, 1), # Usage dropping, customer service call!
    ("SUB-1", "2023-11-20", 0.1, 5,  2), # Severe drop, multiple calls

    ("SUB-2", "2023-11-20", 3.2, 55, 0)
]

schema = "subscriber_id STRING, usage_date STRING, data_gb DOUBLE, call_mins INT, support_calls INT"
df_usage = spark.createDataFrame(daily_usage, schema).withColumn("ts", F.to_date("usage_date"))

# --- Execution Step ---
# Convert date to epoch days for rangeBetween window
df_with_days = df_usage.withColumn("day_num", F.col("ts").cast("date").cast("long"))

# Rolling 30-day window (29 preceding days + current day)
win_30d = Window.partitionBy("subscriber_id").orderBy("day_num").rangeBetween(-29, 0)

df_features = (
    df_with_days
    .withColumn("avg_data_gb_30d", F.round(F.avg("data_gb").over(win_30d), 2))
    .withColumn("total_support_calls_30d", F.sum("support_calls").over(win_30d))
    .withColumn("max_daily_call_mins_30d", F.max("call_mins").over(win_30d))
)

    # Usage ratio: current data vs 30-day average (ratio < 0.5 indicates drop)
    .withColumn(
        "data_usage_drop_ratio",
        F.when(F.col("avg_data_gb_30d") > 0, F.round(F.col("data_gb") / F.col("avg_data_gb_30d"), 2)).otherwise(1.0)
    )
    .withColumn(
        "is_high_churn_risk",
        F.when((F.col("data_usage_drop_ratio") < 0.4) & (F.col("total_support_calls_30d") >= 2), 1).otherwise(0)

        "usage_date",
        "avg_data_gb_30d",
        "total_support_calls_30d",

)

# --- Execution Step ---
raw_logs = [
    ('192.168.1.10 - - [20/Nov/2023:12:00:01 +0000] "GET /index.html HTTP/1.1" 200 4500'),
    ('192.168.1.10 - - [20/Nov/2023:12:00:05 +0000] "GET /about.html HTTP/1.1" 200 2300'),
    # Attack 1: SQL Injection attempt
    ('10.0.0.99 - - [20/Nov/2023:12:01:00 +0000] "GET /login?user=admin\'%20OR%201=1-- HTTP/1.1" 401 520'),
    # Attack 2: Directory traversal attempt
    ('10.0.0.99 - - [20/Nov/2023:12:01:02 +0000] "GET /../../etc/passwd HTTP/1.1" 403 310'),
    # Attack 3: High-frequency brute force
    ('10.0.0.99 - - [20/Nov/2023:12:01:04 +0000] "POST /api/v1/auth HTTP/1.1" 401 120')
]

df_raw_logs = spark.createDataFrame([(l,) for l in raw_logs], ["raw_log"])
df_raw_logs.show(truncate=False)

# --- Execution Step ---
clf_regex = r'^(\S+) \S+ \S+ \[([^\]]+)\] "(\S+) (\S+) \S+" (\d{3}) (\d+)'

df_parsed_logs = (
    df_raw_logs
    .withColumn("client_ip", F.regexp_extract("raw_log", clf_regex, 1))
    .withColumn("request_ts_str", F.regexp_extract("raw_log", clf_regex, 2))
    .withColumn("http_method", F.regexp_extract("raw_log", clf_regex, 3))
    .withColumn("request_uri", F.regexp_extract("raw_log", clf_regex, 4))
    .withColumn("status_code", F.regexp_extract("raw_log", clf_regex, 5).cast(T.IntegerType()))
    .withColumn("bytes_sent", F.regexp_extract("raw_log", clf_regex, 6).cast(T.LongType()))
)

df_parsed_logs.select("client_ip", "http_method", "request_uri", "status_code").show(truncate=False)

# --- Execution Step ---
df_threats = (
    df_parsed_logs
    .withColumn(
        "threat_type",
        F.when(F.lower(F.col("request_uri")).rlike(r"(or%201=1|union%20select|drop%20table)"), "SQL_INJECTION")
         .when(F.col("request_uri").contains("../"), "PATH_TRAVERSAL")
         .when((F.col("status_code") == 401) & (F.col("http_method") == "POST"), "BRUTE_FORCE_AUTH")
         .otherwise(None)
    )
)

print("Identified Cybersecurity Incidents:")
df_threats.filter(F.col("threat_type").isNotNull()).select("client_ip", "request_uri", "status_code", "threat_type").show(truncate=False)

# Build active IP blacklist table
df_blacklist = (
    df_threats
    .filter(F.col("threat_type").isNotNull())
    .groupBy("client_ip")
    .agg(
        F.count("threat_type").alias("incident_count"),
        F.collect_set("threat_type").alias("detected_attacks")
    )

)

print("Automated Firewall IP Blacklist Feed:")
df_blacklist.show(truncate=False)
notes: Log parsing in big data pipelines is CPU-intensive. Using native `regexp_extract()` with pre-compiled regex groups in Catalyst operates inside Tungsten UTF-8 binary format, avoiding Java String object garbage collection pressure.
use_case: A cyber defense operations center monitors 100 million web server access logs daily. Security analysts must parse unformatted Nginx/Apache logs, detect DDoS attacks (IPs generating > 100 requests in 1 minute), identify SQL injection attempts, and geolocate threat origins.

]

    .withColumn("moving_avg", F.round(F.avg("vibration_mm").over(win_machine), 2))

    .withColumn(

            F.round(F.abs(F.col("vibration_mm") - F.col("moving_avg")) / F.col("moving_stddev"), 2)
        ).otherwise(0.0)

    .withColumn(

    )

title: #102 Project Supply Chain: Inventory Replenishment Forecasting and Reorder Triggers
description: Build an automated supply chain replenishment model in PySpark: (1) Compute 14-day moving daily sales velocity, (2) Estimate lead-time demand and safety stock using standard formulas ($SS = Z \times \sigma_{LTD}$), (3) Calculate dynamic Reorder Points (ROP), and (4) Generate automated Purchase Order requisitions.

import os
